title: Mainstreaming Sustainable Land and Forest Management in Mountain Landscapes of North-Eastern Armenia (UNDP/GEF 5353; GEF title: '...in Dry Mountain Landscapes')
summary: UNDP/GEF project in Lori and Tavush marzes, which hold about 65 percent of Armenia's forest resources. It integrated sustainable forest and land management into planning across about 650,000 ha, revised forest management plans, rehabilitated pastures and forests in pilot communities and supported alternative livelihoods and energy for forest-dependent villages.
activities: Revision of forest management plans in six pilot forest enterprise branches (three per marz)
Community-based pasture and fodder improvement and forest-pasture management in six target communities
Forest regeneration, school forest district and sustainable non-timber use (Koghb, Noyemberyan)
Alternative livelihoods and energy (e.g. solar systems at schools and kindergartens, anti-hail stations, efficient stoves)
Dendrochronology and carbon-stock inventory to support national GHG accounting
results: 227 ha under fodder production or improved in the six target communities (Regional Post)

Planning/targets reported in 2017: restoration of degraded forest, about 1,000 ha pastures, about 200,000 ha with improved soil management (Ecolur; the article's headline and body disagree on the forest figure)

Final workshop (6-7 May 2021) presented forest-regeneration results, biofuel market development, alternative livelihoods in Tavush, monitoring of illegal deforestation, dendrochronology and carbon stock inventory with national coefficients

title: MCC / Millennium Challenge Account-Armenia Irrigated Agriculture Project (Infrastructure Activity and Water-to-Market Activity)
summary: The largest irrigation refurbishment in Armenia's history under the MCC Compact. The Infrastructure Activity rehabilitated main canals, pumping stations, gravity systems, tertiary canals and drainage in the Ararat Valley and other regions; the Water-to-Market Activity trained farmers, provided credit and strengthened WUAs and water supply agencies.
activities: Six main canals rehabilitated (41.8 km lined, over 260 structures)
17 irrigation pumping stations rehabilitated; five pump-to-gravity conversions (almost 50 km of canals)
Tertiary canals rehabilitated in more than 100 communities (232.8 km, 15 percent community co-financing)
470 km of drainage canals cleaned in the Ararat and Armavir regions
Support to 44 WUAs and three water supply agencies (management improvement plans, 180 computers with GIS software); farmer training and rural credit (US$12.7 million, 1,008 borrowers)
results: Infrastructure activity ERR 24.4 percent at closure; Mathematica 2016 evaluation found improved water timeliness near tertiary canals but no evidence of higher irrigated area or household income
Water-to-Market: farmer training did not measurably change on-farm water management (2013 evaluation)

title: EU4Sevan - Environmental protection of Lake Sevan (EU and BMZ; UNDP and GIZ)
summary: Joint EU-BMZ programme implemented by UNDP and GIZ under the Ministry of Environment to improve the protection of Lake Sevan: governance and management framework for the lake ecosystem and Sevan National Park, water monitoring capacity, ecosystem-friendly farming and land use, and wastewater treatment using nature-based solutions.
activities: Strengthen water monitoring and management capacity in the Lake Sevan watershed; first River Basin Management Plan for the Sevan basin (supported with EUWI Plus)
Ecosystem-friendly, water-protecting land use and cultivation

GIZ feasibility study (Aug 2021-Jan 2022) of centralised, semi-centralised and decentralised wastewater options near the lake; decentralised wastewater plant commissioned at Kindergarten No. 2, Noratus (22 July 2025)
Awareness raising among basin communities and private sector; COVID-19 fast-track: about 600,000 willow cuttings and fruit trees planted, riverbed waste collected, 750 short-term jobs
results: Decentralised biological wastewater treatment plant at Noratus kindergarten commissioned (22 July 2025)

title: Local Economy and Infrastructure Development Project (LEID)
summary: LEID financed urban regeneration, access roads and visitor facilities at heritage and tourism hubs and sites in several marzes, plus institutional support, to raise tourism's contribution to the local economy. About 38 subprojects were planned across 17 sites.
activities: Heritage hub regeneration: public spaces, facades, access roads, water and sanitation, street lighting
Tourism circuits: site preservation, visitor facilities (information centres, toilets, parking)
Institutional development: destination management organisations, site management plans, business advisory services
June 2020 restructuring added Aragatsotn, Gegharkunik and Tavush; COVID-19 medical supplies for Martuni and Vayots Dzor medical centres
results: 1,023 temporary construction jobs and 350 follow-on private-sector jobs (IEG review)
67.5 km of improved access roads to tourism sites; 1,453 street lighting posts; 4 urban parks upgraded (2 in Gyumri, 1 Goris, 1 Tsaghkunk); 29 tourist facilities at 11 sites

title: GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) Armenia - all operational phases (UNDP)
summary: The GEF Small Grants Programme in Armenia, delivered by UNDP, funds small community and NGO projects in biodiversity, climate change, land degradation, chemicals and waste and capacity development. It started in 2009 and had committed 120 projects by 2023, with UNDP estimating projects in more than 70 rural communities. It is currently in its eighth operational phase (OP8).
activities: Grants to NGOs and community groups for community conservation, eco-corridors and ecotourism
Renewable energy, energy efficiency and sustainable transport pilots
Sustainable land management on small farms (e.g. greenhouses, orchards, irrigation)
results: By 2023: 120 projects; at least 10,000 households and more than 70 rural communities benefited per a 2019 UNDP country evaluation (estimates by the UNDP office)
FY2016-2023: 12 biodiversity and 12 land degradation projects completed; 6 protected areas positively influenced covering 8,181 ha

title: World Bank Municipal Water and Wastewater Project (with Additional Financing)
summary: The project supported the financial and technical rehabilitation of water services run by the Armenia Water and Sewerage Company outside Yerevan. It financed management support, investments in branch water systems of 14 small towns plus immediate works in Dilijan and Sevan, and pipe and meter replacement.
activities: Immediate investments: rehabilitation of two water treatment plants in Dilijan, two new water reservoirs in Sevan and replacement of leaky pipes in both cities
Main investment program: 10 pumping stations, 13 storage reservoirs and 221 km of distribution pipes in 14 urban areas
Management contract and institutional support for AWSC; Additional Financing for water network of Hrazdan city and feasibility studies for two towns' wastewater systems
results: 94 percent of cities and towns in AWSC service areas reported at least minimum water-supply hours at completion (ICR)

title: Living Landscapes for Market Development in Armenia (LILA, Swiss SDC / WWF Armenia), Phase 1
summary: SDC-funded project implemented by WWF Armenia to raise incomes of farmers and rural businesses in remote mountain communities while protecting natural resources and biodiversity. Phase 1 concluded on 21 November 2025 after working in seven consolidated communities in Tavush, Lori, Vayots Dzor and Syunik.
activities: Pasture management plans and 21 pasture infrastructure units
Solar PV and water heaters on public buildings in communities
Support to 31 tourism and related rural businesses; gastro-tourism yards and small production units
196 ha put under sustainable management, including 148 ha of forest
results: 508 households received additional income; 31 businesses supported employing about 700 people
Nearly 70,000 visitors benefited from improved infrastructure; over 13,000 people benefited from climate-related initiatives; 102 t CO2 emissions prevented

title: Scaling up national adaptive capacities for climate change-driven natural hazards through strengthening monitoring and early warning systems (GCF SAP068)
summary: EPIU is the accredited entity for a Green Climate Fund project to build a people-centred, national multi-hazard early warning system for Armenia. It modernises meteorological and hydrological observation and forecasting, strengthens multi-channel early-warning dissemination, and develops resilience-financing tools such as forecast-based financing and climate micro-insurance. The GCF page targets about 1.07 million direct beneficiaries.
activities: Modernise meteorological and hydrological observation and forecasting systems
Multi-channel early-warning dissemination and risk communication, including inclusive warnings for about 300,000 vulnerable people
Resilience-financing mechanisms: forecast-based financing and climate micro-insurance

title: USAID Armenia Improved Water Management for Sustainable Economic Growth Program
summary: Five-year USAID programme to change how Armenia manages water: advanced analytical tools and data for water allocation, governance reform, promotion of water-conservation practices and technologies, access to water and preparation for regional cooperation.
activities: Apply advanced technologies and tools for sustainable water management; strengthen data-driven allocation decisions in the Ministry of Environment
Improve water governance

Demonstrate water conservation technologies; improve access to water (launch coverage: drinking and irrigation water for about 20,000 residents, model networks, meters and modernisation of 10 observation points)
Political economy analysis of the water sector (AUA Acopian Center, 2023-24); technical support for the Southern basin management plan

title: Emergency agricultural inputs support to the most vulnerable smallholder farmers (Ukraine conflict supply disruption; NK refugee households)
summary: In response to input supply disruption after the war in Ukraine, FAO delivered high-quality winter wheat seed and advice to the most vulnerable smallholders in Gegharkunik, Shirak and Syunik in October 2022. The project title also covers livelihood support to refugee households from Nagorno-Karabakh, for which no locations were found.
activities: Import and distribution of winter wheat seed (301 t planned for 1,078 beneficiaries, up to 300 kg each)
Leaflets and consultations on winter wheat cultivation
results: 151 t of winter wheat seed already distributed by 8 October 2022 in Gegharkunik and Shirak communities (FAO); UN Joint SDG Fund annual report later cited a lower figure (91 t to 304 farmers) - not verified

title: World Bank Municipal Water Project (Masis, Ashtarak, Echmiadzin)
summary: The project rehabilitated water networks in the towns of Masis, Ashtarak and Echmiadzin and their neighbouring rural settlements to cut losses and improve service, and financed meters and pumping-station automation across the AWSC service area.
activities: Component 1: rehabilitation and sectorisation of water networks in Masis, Echmiadzin and Ashtarak and neighbouring villages (non-revenue water reduction)
Component 2: water-meter replacement and meter chambers in several cities and villages, automation of pumping stations and reservoirs (e.g. Masis), equipment for AWSC
More than 9,000 individual meters installed in the three towns
results: Water-supply improvements and beneficiary surveys carried out in Masis, Ashtarak and Echmiadzin

title: USAID Advanced Science and Partnerships for Integrated Resource Development (ASPIRED)
summary: USAID activity to reduce groundwater extraction in the Ararat Valley to sustainable levels through science, technology and partnerships. It piloted water-conservation technologies on fish farms and built groundwater tools with the US Geological Survey for the Ararat Basin.
activities: Pilot water-conservation technologies at fish farms (flow meters and data loggers on 19 water-use points at four fisheries, per search coverage)
USGS characterisation of the Ararat Basin hydrogeological framework and design of a groundwater monitoring network
Science-based tools: groundwater model, decision support system for the Ararat Valley catchment, online groundwater use monitoring (IATI description)

title: EU4BiodiversityinSevan: Enhancing Lake Sevan Ecosystem Restoration
summary: Three-year EU-funded UNDP project to create conditions for long-term restoration and management of the Lake Sevan ecosystem: governance and institutional capacity, riverbank and riverbed restoration for Sevan trout, forest-cover assessment for the basin, sustainable fisheries and financing of Sevan National Park.
activities: Digital tools for biodiversity monitoring and reporting
Assessment of the industrial fishing value chain and sustainable fisheries management
Riverbank and riverbed restoration to support Sevan Salmo populations
Forest cover assessment and revision of forest rehabilitation plans for the Lake Sevan basin
Financial sustainability of Sevan National Park through recreational development

title: Advanced Rural Development Initiative (ARDI)
summary: ARDI was a USAID rural economic development programme supporting dairy, fruit processing and rural tourism enterprises and small infrastructure in selected rural communities. It was launched in January 2014 alongside the Partnerships for Rural Prosperity programme.
activities: Milk collection units, milk processing plants, herbal tea production, farmer service centres, animal watering points, upgraded bed and breakfasts, dry fruit production (17 projects in 2017)
Small-scale infrastructure and seed grants for youth- and women-led start-ups
results: Fuller Center reports 70 infrastructure projects and 100 seed grants since 2017 (self-reported)

title: Sustainable Energy for climate resilient municipal development in Armenia (SE4Resilience)
summary: SE4Resilience promotes renewable energy and energy efficiency in households and public buildings of rural communities in Tavush, Shirak, Gegharkunik and Syunik, to reduce energy poverty and improve climate resilience. It is included for its rural spatial footprint although it is an energy programme.
activities: Efficient stoves, insulation, solar thermal heaters and PV in low-income households and community buildings
Capacity of rural municipalities to pilot renewable energy and efficiency in public infrastructure
Gender-sensitive competence development

title: Capacity building in forestry and establishment of agroforestry concepts (BMZ-funded expert advisory)
summary: Two BMZ-funded expert-advisory activities on forestry in Armenia: capacity building in forestry (2021-2025) and, from 2025, establishing agroforestry concepts on community-owned land, building on pilot reforestation projects in different geographical and climatic zones. The expert advises on training materials, courses, networks and advocacy.
activities: Capacity building in forestry
Advice on training materials and courses, networks and advocacy for agroforestry; mixed-forest establishment on community-owned land

title: ADB Sevan-Hrazdan Cascade Hydropower System Rehabilitation Project (Loan 2996)
summary: A US$25 million ADB private sector loan helped rehabilitate and modernise four hydropower plants of the Sevan-Hrazdan cascade, which runs along the Hrazdan River from Lake Sevan to Yerevan, restoring 45 MW of capacity. The cascade uses Lake Sevan outflow and so interacts with lake-level management.
activities: Rehabilitation and modernisation of four hydropower plants of the cascade
Plugging leaks in diversion channels (press)
results: 45 MW of generation capacity restored; improved safety and reliability (ADB results page)

title: Kotayk Solid Waste Project (Hrazdan regional landfill for Kotayk and Gegharkunik)
summary: The project built the first EU-compliant sanitary landfill in Armenia, in Hrazdan, serving twelve municipalities of Kotayk and Gegharkunik and about 500,000 people. The landfill opened on 8 July 2025.
activities: Construction of a sanitary landfill in Hrazdan managed commercially
Waste collection and disposal for twelve participating municipalities
Corporate development of the landfill company (Austrian support)
results: New landfill opened 8 July 2025 to serve Kotayk and Gegharkunik (EU Delegation)

title: High-Efficiency Horticulture and Integrated Supply Chain Project (Spayka greenhouses)
summary: ADB lent USD 32 million to Spayka LLC to develop about 30 ha of climate-controlled greenhouses with drip irrigation in Yerevan, growing tomatoes and bell peppers for export to Russia and the UAE. This is a private-sector investment, not a rural community programme.
activities: Build about 30 ha of climate-controlled greenhouses with drip irrigation
Export tomatoes and bell peppers (Russia, UAE) through Spayka's existing supply chain

title: Yerevan Solid Waste Project (Nubarashen landfill closure and new sanitary landfill) - cancelled
summary: The project planned to reclaim the existing Nubarashen landfill and build an EU-compliant sanitary landfill nearby for Yerevan. EcoLur reports that the project was cancelled, and Yerevan Municipality has since sought other finance (World Bank, EBRD, ADB).
activities: Construction of an EU-compliant landfill for Yerevan (city of 1.1 million) with gas capture (planned)
Reclamation of Nubarashen landfill (planned)

title: STRIVE for a better future: communities and civil society resilience in Armenia
summary: STRIVE strengthens Armenian civil society organisations and funds community initiatives through competitive and emergency sub-grants. It is geographically balanced across the country but works on civil society capacity, not on a defined territory.
activities: Capacity building for CSOs
Sub-grants for community development, women's rights, disability, green transition and youth

title: Sustainable Land Management for Increased Productivity in Armenia (SLMIP, GEF 8005, IFAD)
summary: GEF-financed land-management component added to IFAD's rural infrastructure and finance programme in Armenia. Its stated aim is to enhance the resilience of rural communities living in risk-prone areas. Closed in 2023.
activities: Sustainable land management and restoration of degraded land in rural communities (details not retrieved)

title: MCF Disaster Risk Reduction Armenia 2026-2029
summary: Swedish-funded programme of disaster risk reduction support to Armenia for 2026-2029, delivered through the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency. The IATI record has no description beyond the title and gives no sites.
